title: Two conjectures of Wormald on Hamilton cycles in tournaments: paper and checking programs
description:
Final revision of the paper, single column, 12 pages, with its LaTeX source and the programs that check its identities on small cases. The paper proves Conjectures 2 and 6 of N. C. Wormald, Tournaments with many Hamilton cycles (arXiv:2610.16245): for a regular tournament on d vertices with skew adjacency matrix S, Wormald's Hessian determinant is H = d det(d^2 I + S^2)/det(d^2 I - S^2), so H is nonzero and d/H is the square of a rational number; for the cyclic tournaments sqrt(d/H) = ((d+1)^d + (d-1)^d)/((d+i)^d + (d-i)^d), which tends to cosh 1 / cos 1 = 2.8559578925..., the constant Wormald estimated. Every statement is proved by hand; no statement rests on the programs.

The results were first made public on 14 October 2026 as release v1.0.0 of creelie/Breakthrough-problems-1 (later versions archived under the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23567152). An earlier and incomplete version of the paper appeared on Hexagon as hexagon:2610.00460.
